records.title: Fixed-Point Quantization Aware Training for on-Device Keyword-Spotting
records.reason: Fixed-point QAT combines squashed weight distributions and cosine regularization and quantizes transient variables for keyword-spotting models. Google Speech Commands and an in-house KWS set report 4-bit accuracy retention and 68% shorter execution time with fixed-point inference. This is a concrete embedded quantization method but for convolutional audio KWS, not transformer/LLM inference; linked low-bit relation is weak.

records.title: AutoTemplate: A Simple Recipe for Lexically Constrained Text Generation
records.reason: AutoTemplate separates constrained generation into template generation and lexicalization, evaluating keyword-to-sentence generation and entity-guided summarization against constraint-satisfaction baselines. It targets lexical constraint quality rather than inference compute, memory, or latency; relation to iterative non-autoregressive generation is task-level only.

records.title: Multi-View Attention Multiple-Instance Learning Enhanced by LLM Reasoning for Cognitive Distortion Detection
records.reason: The framework decomposes utterances into emotion, logic and behavior elements, applies LLM reasoning and gated multi-view MIL for cognitive-distortion classification. Evaluation on Korean and English mental-health datasets measures classification quality. It is a task-specific LLM application, not inference efficiency or compression; the linked MiniLM paper is unrelated technically.

records.title: HadamRNN: Binary and Sparse Ternary Orthogonal RNNs
records.reason: HadamRNN parameterizes orthogonal recurrent matrices with binary or sparse-ternary weights and evaluates copy, MNIST, IMDB, GLUE and IoT tasks. It reports near full-precision task quality with compact low-bit recurrent weights. The approach is RNN-specific and not transformer/LLM inference; BERT quantization linkage is a weak low-bit analogy.

records.title: Poor-Supervised Evaluation for SuperLLM via Mutual Consistency
records.reason: PoEM evaluates LLM capability without reliable labels by alternating model/human reference calibration and filtering. Experiments across 3 task types and 16 LLMs report 0.98 average Pearson correlation with supervised evaluation. The contribution is an evaluation method, not inference optimization; the linked test-time scaling paper is only a shared evaluation context.
